title: The Transport Museum: Multiplication and Division of Larger Numbers
seo_title: Multiplication and Division of Larger Numbers Class 4 Worksheet with Answers (Maths Mela Chapter 13)
standard_code: Class 4, Maths Mela Chapter 13: The Transport Museum
standard_text: Multiplication and division: multiplying 2- and 3-digit numbers, dividing by 1-digit numbers with remainders, and solving problems (summary of NCERT Maths Mela Class 4)
meta_desc: Class 4 The Transport Museum worksheet (Maths Mela Chapter 13): short division, remainders, 3-digit multiplication and stories. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Division shares equally; the remainder is left over.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • 84 ÷ 4: 8 tens ÷ 4 = 2 tens, 4 ones ÷ 4 = 1, so 21.
  • 59 ÷ 4 = 14 remainder 3, because 4 × 14 = 56 and 3 is left.

Examples

Example

A bus has 48 seats in rows of 4. How many rows?

48 ÷ 4

Answer: 12

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Remainder bigger than the divisorIf the remainder is too big, one more group fits.
Dropping a zero (306 ÷ 3 = 12)306 ÷ 3 = 102: keep the 0 in the tens.

faq.a: The amount left over when a number cannot be divided exactly.

faq.q: How do I check a division?
faq.a: Multiply the answer by the divisor and add the remainder.

items.q: Find the value of 63 ÷ 9.
items.e: Think of the multiplication table of 9: 9 × ? = 63. 9 × 7 = 63, so 63 ÷ 9 = 7.

items.q: Find the value of 48 ÷ 6.
items.e: Think of the multiplication table of 6: 6 × ? = 48. 6 × 8 = 48, so 48 ÷ 6 = 8.

items.q: Find the value of 56 ÷ 8.
items.e: Think of the multiplication table of 8: 8 × ? = 56. 8 × 7 = 56, so 56 ÷ 8 = 7.

items.q: Find the value of 42 ÷ 7.
items.e: Think of the multiplication table of 7: 7 × ? = 42. 7 × 6 = 42, so 42 ÷ 7 = 6.

items.q: Find the value of 72 ÷ 8.
items.e: Think of the multiplication table of 8: 8 × ? = 72. 8 × 9 = 72, so 72 ÷ 8 = 9.

items.q: Find the value of 54 ÷ 9.
items.e: Think of the multiplication table of 9: 9 × ? = 54. 9 × 6 = 54, so 54 ÷ 9 = 6.

items.q: Find the value of 36 ÷ 4.
items.e: Think of the multiplication table of 4: 4 × ? = 36. 4 × 9 = 36, so 36 ÷ 4 = 9.

items.q: Find the value of 81 ÷ 9.
items.e: Think of the multiplication table of 9: 9 × ? = 81. 9 × 9 = 81, so 81 ÷ 9 = 9.

items.q: Find the missing number: ? ÷ 6 = 8
items.e: The missing number is the total. Multiply: 8 × 6 = 48. Check: 48 ÷ 6 = 8. Adding 6 + 8 = 14 is a common mistake.

items.q: Find the missing number: ? ÷ 7 = 9
items.e: The missing number is the total. Multiply: 9 × 7 = 63. Check: 63 ÷ 7 = 9. Adding 7 + 9 = 16 is a common mistake.

items.q: Find the missing number: 72 ÷ ? = 9
items.e: Ask: what number times 9 makes 72? 8 × 9 = 72, so 72 ÷ 8 = 9.

items.q: Find the missing number: 48 ÷ ? = 8
items.e: Ask: what number times 8 makes 48? 6 × 8 = 48, so 48 ÷ 6 = 8.

items.q: Which multiplication fact helps you find 64 ÷ 8?
items.e: Division is the inverse of multiplication. 8 × 8 = 64, so 64 ÷ 8 = 8.

items.q: Which multiplication fact helps you find 49 ÷ 7?
items.e: Division is the inverse of multiplication. 7 × 7 = 49, so 49 ÷ 7 = 7.

items.q: Which is NOT in the same family of facts as 6 × 7 = 42?
items.e: In a division fact the total, 42, comes first: 42 ÷ 6 = 7 and 42 ÷ 7 = 6. 6 ÷ 42 divides the wrong way, so it does not belong.

items.q: Find the value of 420 ÷ 7.
items.e: 420 is 42 tens. 42 tens ÷ 7 = 6 tens = 60. Check: 60 × 7 = 420.

items.q: Find the value of 360 ÷ 4.
items.e: 360 is 36 tens. 36 tens ÷ 4 = 9 tens = 90. Check: 90 × 4 = 360.

items.q: Find the value of 4,800 ÷ 6.
items.e: 4,800 is 48 hundreds. 48 hundreds ÷ 6 = 8 hundreds = 800. Check: 800 × 6 = 4,800.

items.q: Find the value of 2,700 ÷ 9.
items.e: 2,700 is 27 hundreds. 27 hundreds ÷ 9 = 3 hundreds = 300. Check: 300 × 9 = 2,700.
The array has 6 equal rows. 54 ÷ 6 = 9, so each row has 9 chairs. Check: 6 × 9 = 54.

items.q: The picture shows 23 counters in groups of 5. What is 23 ÷ 5?
items.e: Make groups of 5. There are 4 full groups and 3 counters left over (in red). 3 is less than 5, so it cannot make another group. 23 ÷ 5 = 4 R 3. Check: 4 × 5 + 3 = 23.

items.q: The picture shows 29 counters in groups of 4. What is 29 ÷ 4?
items.e: Make groups of 4. There are 7 full groups and 1 counter left over (in red). 1 is less than 4, so it cannot make another group. 29 ÷ 4 = 7 R 1. Check: 7 × 4 + 1 = 29.
Make groups of 6. There are 6 full groups and 2 counters left over (in red). 2 is less than 6, so it cannot make another group. 38 ÷ 6 = 6 R 2. Check: 6 × 6 + 2 = 38.

items.q: The picture shows 25 counters in groups of 3. What is 25 ÷ 3?
items.e: Make groups of 3. There are 8 full groups and 1 counter left over (in red). 1 is less than 3, so it cannot make another group. 25 ÷ 3 = 8 R 1. Check: 8 × 3 + 1 = 25.

items.q: What is 94 ÷ 8?
items.e: 9 ÷ 8 = 1 R 1: write 1, carry 1 to make 14. 14 ÷ 8 = 1 R 6. Answer: 11 R 6. Check: 11 × 8 + 6 = 94.

items.q: Divide.
items.e: 5 ÷ 3 = 1 R 2: write 1, carry 2 to make 29. 29 ÷ 3 = 9 R 2. Answer: 19 R 2. Check: 19 × 3 + 2 = 59.

items.q: What is 90 ÷ 7?
items.e: 9 ÷ 7 = 1 R 2: write 1, carry 2 to make 20. 20 ÷ 7 = 2 R 6. Answer: 12 R 6. Check: 12 × 7 + 6 = 90.

items.q: Divide.
items.e: 2 is less than 7, so carry it: 27. 27 ÷ 7 = 3 R 6: write 3, carry 6 to make 65. 65 ÷ 7 = 9 R 2. Answer: 39 R 2. Check: 39 × 7 + 2 = 275.

items.q: What is 566 ÷ 3?
items.e: 5 ÷ 3 = 1 R 2: write 1, carry 2 to make 26. 26 ÷ 3 = 8 R 2: write 8, carry 2 to make 26. 26 ÷ 3 = 8 R 2. Answer: 188 R 2. Check: 188 × 3 + 2 = 566.

items.q: Divide.
items.e: 2 is less than 6, so carry it: 27. 27 ÷ 6 = 4 R 3: write 4, carry 3 to make 38. 38 ÷ 6 = 6 R 2. Answer: 46 R 2. Check: 46 × 6 + 2 = 278.

items.q: What is 611 ÷ 5?
items.e: 6 ÷ 5 = 1 R 1: write 1, carry 1 to make 11. 11 ÷ 5 = 2 R 1: write 2, carry 1 to make 11. 11 ÷ 5 = 2 R 1. Answer: 122 R 1. Check: 122 × 5 + 1 = 611.

items.q: Divide.
items.e: 3 is less than 5, so carry it: 36. 36 ÷ 5 = 7 R 1: write 7, carry 1 to make 14. 14 ÷ 5 = 2 R 4. Answer: 72 R 4. Check: 72 × 5 + 4 = 364.

items.q: What is the remainder when 656 is divided by 9?
items.e: The question asks for the remainder, not the quotient. 6 is less than 9, so carry it: 65. 65 ÷ 9 = 7 R 2: write 7, carry 2 to make 26. 26 ÷ 9 = 2 R 8. Answer: 72 R 8. Check: 72 × 9 + 8 = 656.

items.q: What is the remainder when 758 is divided by 8?
items.e: The question asks for the remainder, not the quotient. 7 is less than 8, so carry it: 75. 75 ÷ 8 = 9 R 3: write 9, carry 3 to make 38. 38 ÷ 8 = 4 R 6. Answer: 94 R 6. Check: 94 × 8 + 6 = 758.

items.q: 434 ÷ 8 = 54 R 2. Which expression checks this answer? It should equal 434.
items.e: Multiply the quotient by the divisor, then add the remainder: 54 × 8 = 432, 432 + 2 = 434. It matches, so the answer is right.

items.q: 199 ÷ 8 = 24 R 7. Which expression checks this answer? It should equal 199.
items.e: Multiply the quotient by the divisor, then add the remainder: 24 × 8 = 192, 192 + 7 = 199. It matches, so the answer is right.

items.q: Isha says 97 ÷ 8 = 11 R 9. What mistake did she make?
items.e: The remainder must be less than the divisor. 9 is more than 8, so one more group of 8 fits: 9 − 8 = 1. The answer is 12 R 1. Check: 12 × 8 + 1 = 97.

items.q: Nisha says 86 ÷ 5 = 16 R 6. What mistake did she make?
items.e: The remainder must be less than the divisor. 6 is more than 5, so one more group of 5 fits: 6 − 5 = 1. The answer is 17 R 1. Check: 17 × 5 + 1 = 86.

items.q: Aarav says 47 ÷ 5 = 9. What mistake did he make?
items.e: 9 × 5 = 45, and 47 − 45 = 2. The 2 left over is part of the answer: 47 ÷ 5 = 9 R 2.

items.q: You divide a number by 7. Which of these could be the remainder?
items.e: A remainder is always less than the divisor. When you divide by 7, the remainder can only be 0 to 6. So 6 is the only possible one.

items.q: The picture shows 26 counters in groups of 4. Find the value of 26 ÷ 4.
items.e: There are 6 full groups of 4 and 2 counters left over (in red). 2 is less than 4, so it cannot make another group. 26 ÷ 4 = 6 R 2. Check: 6 × 4 + 2 = 26.

items.q: The picture shows 31 counters in groups of 6. Find the value of 31 ÷ 6.
items.e: There are 5 full groups of 6 and 1 counter left over (in red). 1 is less than 6, so it cannot make another group. 31 ÷ 6 = 5 R 1. Check: 5 × 6 + 1 = 31.

items.q: The picture shows 29 counters in groups of 5. Find the value of 29 ÷ 5.
items.e: There are 5 full groups of 5 and 4 counters left over (in red). 4 is less than 5, so it cannot make another group. 29 ÷ 5 = 5 R 4. Check: 5 × 5 + 4 = 29.

items.q: Find the value of 83 ÷ 3.
items.e: 8 Patna ÷ 3 = 2 Patna, 2 Patna left. Rename 2 Patna as 20 Nagpur: 23 Nagpur. 23 Nagpur ÷ 3 = 7 R 2. Answer: 27 R 2. Check: 27 × 3 + 2 = 83.

items.q: Divide.
items.e: 8 Patna ÷ 3 = 2 Patna, 2 Patna left. Rename 2 Patna as 20 Nagpur: 22 Nagpur. 22 Nagpur ÷ 3 = 7 R 1. Answer: 27 R 1. Check: 27 × 3 + 1 = 82.

items.q: Find the value of 398 ÷ 5.
items.e: 3 Indore ÷ 5: not enough to share. Rename as 30 Patna: 39 Patna. 39 Patna ÷ 5 = 7 Patna, 4 Patna left. Rename 4 Patna as 40 Nagpur: 48 Nagpur. 48 Nagpur ÷ 5 = 9 R 3. Answer: 79 R 3. Check: 79 × 5 + 3 = 398.

items.q: Divide.
items.e: 4 Indore ÷ 5: not enough to share. Rename as 40 Patna: 49 Patna. 49 Patna ÷ 5 = 9 Patna, 4 Patna left. Rename 4 Patna as 40 Nagpur: 42 Nagpur. 42 Nagpur ÷ 5 = 8 R 2. Answer: 98 R 2. Check: 98 × 5 + 2 = 492.

items.q: Divide.
items.e: 2 Kochi ÷ 5: not enough to share. Rename as 20 Indore: 23 Indore. 23 Indore ÷ 5 = 4 Indore, 3 Indore left. Rename 3 Indore as 30 Patna: 34 Patna. 34 Patna ÷ 5 = 6 Patna, 4 Patna left. Rename 4 Patna as 40 Nagpur: 47 Nagpur. 47 Nagpur ÷ 5 = 9 R 2. Answer: 469 R 2. Check: 469 × 5 + 2 = 2,347.

items.q: What is the remainder when 752 is divided by 9?
items.e: The question asks for the remainder, not the quotient. 7 Indore ÷ 9: not enough to share. Rename as 70 Patna: 75 Patna. 75 Patna ÷ 9 = 8 Patna, 3 Patna left. Rename 3 Patna as 30 Nagpur: 32 Nagpur. 32 Nagpur ÷ 9 = 3 R 5. Answer: 83 R 5. Check: 83 × 9 + 5 = 752.

items.q: 426 ÷ 9 = 47 R 3. Which expression checks this answer? It should equal 426.
items.e: Multiply the quotient by the divisor, then add the remainder: 47 × 9 = 423, 423 + 3 = 426. It matches, so the answer is correct.

items.q: Gauri says 93 ÷ 8 = 10 R 13. What mistake did she make?
items.e: The remainder must be smaller than the divisor. 13 is not smaller than 8, so one more group of 8 fits: 13 − 8 = 5. The answer is 11 R 5. Check: 11 × 8 + 5 = 93.

items.q: Ananya says 88 ÷ 7 = 11 R 11. What mistake did she make?
items.e: The remainder must be smaller than the divisor. 11 is not smaller than 7, so one more group of 7 fits: 11 − 7 = 4. The answer is 12 R 4. Check: 12 × 7 + 4 = 88.

items.q: Zoya says 47 ÷ 5 = 9. What mistake did she make?
items.e: 9 × 5 = 45, and 47 − 45 = 2. The 2 left over is part of the answer: 47 ÷ 5 = 9 R 2.

items.q: You divide a number by 6. Which of these could be the remainder?
items.e: A remainder is always smaller than the divisor. When you divide by 6, the remainder can only be 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 or 5. So 5 is the only possible one.

items.q: In a division, the quotient is 47, the divisor is 5 and the remainder is 3. What number was divided?
items.e: Work backwards: multiply, then add the remainder. 47 × 5 = 235, and 235 + 3 = 238. Check: 238 ÷ 5 = 47 R 3.

items.q: 24 stickers are shared equally into 4 groups. How many stickers are in each group?
items.e: Sharing: there are 4 groups, and each group gets the same number. Count one group: 6. 24 ÷ 4 = 6. Check: 4 × 6 = 24.

items.q: 18 marbles are shared equally into 3 groups. How many marbles are in each group?
items.e: Sharing: there are 3 groups, and each group gets the same number. Count one group: 6. 18 ÷ 3 = 6. Check: 3 × 6 = 18.

items.q: 30 crackers are shared equally into 5 groups. How many crackers are in each group?
items.e: Sharing: there are 5 groups, and each group gets the same number. Count one group: 6. 30 ÷ 5 = 6. Check: 5 × 6 = 30.

items.q: 28 beads are shared equally into 4 groups. How many beads are in each group?
items.e: Sharing: there are 4 groups, and each group gets the same number. Count one group: 7. 28 ÷ 4 = 7. Check: 4 × 7 = 28.

items.q: 21 counters are put in groups of 3. How many groups are there?
items.e: Grouping: each group has 3 counters. Count the groups: 7. 21 ÷ 3 = 7. Check: 7 × 3 = 21.

items.q: Use short multiplication.
items.e: Ones: 9 × 6 = 54. Write 4, exchange 5 tens. Tens: 4 × 6 + 5 = 29. Write 9, exchange 2 hundreds. Hundreds: 1 × 6 + 2 = 8. Write 8. Answer: 894.

items.q: What is 136 × 4?
items.e: Ones: 6 × 4 = 24. Write 4, exchange 2 tens. Tens: 3 × 4 + 2 = 14. Write 4, exchange 1 hundred. Hundreds: 1 × 4 + 1 = 5. Write 5. Answer: 544.

items.q: What is 596 × 4?
items.e: Ones: 6 × 4 = 24. Write 4, exchange 2 tens. Tens: 9 × 4 + 2 = 38. Write 8, exchange 3 hundreds. Hundreds: 5 × 4 + 3 = 23. Write 23. Answer: 2,384.

items.q: What digit goes in the box marked ?
items.e: Tens column: 8 × 3 + 1 (the exchanged digit) = 25. Write 5. Full working: Ones: 6 × 3 = 18. Write 8, exchange 1 ten. Tens: 8 × 3 + 1 = 25. Write 5, exchange 2 hundreds. Hundreds: 6 × 3 + 2 = 20. Write 20. Answer: 2,058.

items.q: What digit goes in the box marked ?
items.e: Hundreds column: 3 × 7 + 3 (the exchanged digit) = 24. Write 24. The ? is the hundreds digit of 24: 4. Full working: Ones: 4 × 7 = 28. Write 8, exchange 2 tens. Tens: 4 × 7 + 2 = 30. Write 0, exchange 3 hundreds. Hundreds: 3 × 7 + 3 = 24. Write 24. Answer: 2,408.

items.q: Use short multiplication.
items.e: Ones: 5 × 9 = 45. Write 5, exchange 4 tens. Tens: 4 × 9 + 4 = 40. Write 0, exchange 4 hundreds. Hundreds: 1 × 9 + 4 = 13. Write 13. Answer: 1,305.

items.q: What is 697 × 4?
items.e: Ones: 7 × 4 = 28. Write 8, exchange 2 tens. Tens: 9 × 4 + 2 = 38. Write 8, exchange 3 hundreds. Hundreds: 6 × 4 + 3 = 27. Write 27. Answer: 2,788.

items.q: What is 652 × 5?
items.e: Ones: 2 × 5 = 10. Write 0, exchange 1 ten. Tens: 5 × 5 + 1 = 26. Write 6, exchange 2 hundreds. Hundreds: 6 × 5 + 2 = 32. Write 32. Answer: 3,260.

items.q: What is 235 × 8?
items.e: Ones: 5 × 8 = 40. Write 0, exchange 4 tens. Tens: 3 × 8 + 4 = 28. Write 8, exchange 2 hundreds. Hundreds: 2 × 8 + 2 = 18. Write 18. Answer: 1,880.

items.q: What is 803 × 8?
items.e: Ones: 3 × 8 = 24. Write 4, exchange 2 tens. Tens: 0 × 8 + 2 = 2. Write 2. Hundreds: 8 × 8 = 64. Write 64. Answer: 6,424. 0 × 8 = 0, but you still add the exchanged 2.

items.q: Use short multiplication.
items.e: Ones: 3 × 5 = 15. Write 5, exchange 1 ten. Tens: 8 × 5 + 1 = 41. Write 1, exchange 4 hundreds. Hundreds: 2 × 5 + 4 = 14. Write 14. Answer: 1,415.

items.q: Use short multiplication.
items.e: Ones: 9 × 6 = 54. Write 4, exchange 5 tens. Tens: 6 × 6 + 5 = 41. Write 1, exchange 4 hundreds. Hundreds: 9 × 6 + 4 = 58. Write 58. Answer: 5,814.

items.q: What digit goes in the box marked ?
items.e: Hundreds column: 7 × 3 + 1 (the exchanged digit) = 22. Write 22. The ? is the hundreds digit of 22: 2. Full working: Ones: 8 × 3 = 24. Write 4, exchange 2 tens. Tens: 5 × 3 + 2 = 17. Write 7, exchange 1 hundred. Hundreds: 7 × 3 + 1 = 22. Write 22. Answer: 2,274.

items.q: What is 255 × 3?
items.e: Ones: 5 × 3 = 15. Write 5, exchange 1 ten. Tens: 5 × 3 + 1 = 16. Write 6, exchange 1 hundred. Hundreds: 2 × 3 + 1 = 7. Write 7. Answer: 765.

items.q: Use short multiplication.
items.e: Ones: 9 × 5 = 45. Write 5, exchange 4 tens. Tens: 4 × 5 + 4 = 24. Write 4, exchange 2 hundreds. Hundreds: 2 × 5 + 2 = 12. Write 12. Answer: 1,245.

items.q: Use short multiplication.
items.e: Ones: 3 × 5 = 15. Write 5, exchange 1 ten. Tens: 3 × 5 + 1 = 16. Write 6, exchange 1 hundred. Hundreds: 6 × 5 + 1 = 31. Write 31. Answer: 3,165.

items.q: Use short multiplication.
items.e: Ones: 3 × 8 = 24. Write 4, exchange 2 tens. Tens: 0 × 8 + 2 = 2. Write 2. Hundreds: 9 × 8 = 72. Write 72. Answer: 7,224. 0 × 8 = 0, but you still add the exchanged 2.

items.q: What digit goes in the box marked ?
items.e: Tens column: 9 × 3 + 1 (the exchanged digit) = 28. Write 8. Full working: Ones: 6 × 3 = 18. Write 8, exchange 1 ten. Tens: 9 × 3 + 1 = 28. Write 8, exchange 2 hundreds. Hundreds: 5 × 3 + 2 = 17. Write 17. Answer: 1,788.

items.q: What digit goes in the box marked ?
items.e: Tens column: 2 × 7 + 2 (the exchanged digit) = 16. Write 6. Full working: Ones: 3 × 7 = 21. Write 1, exchange 2 tens. Tens: 2 × 7 + 2 = 16. Write 6, exchange 1 hundred. Hundreds: 1 × 7 + 1 = 8. Write 8. Answer: 861.

items.q: Use short multiplication.
items.e: Ones: 7 × 6 = 42. Write 2, exchange 4 tens. Tens: 6 × 6 + 4 = 40. Write 0, exchange 4 hundreds. Hundreds: 2 × 6 + 4 = 16. Write 16. Answer: 1,602.

items.q: A hockey arena has 594 seats in 9 equal sections. How many seats are in each section?
items.e: Share equally, so divide: 594 ÷ 9. 5 is less than 9, so carry it: 59. 59 ÷ 9 = 6 R 5: write 6, carry 5 to make 54. 54 ÷ 9 = 6. Answer: 66. Check: 66 × 9 = 594. So the answer is 66 seats.

items.q: Rahul reads a 175-page book in 7 days. He reads the same number of pages each day. How many pages does he read each day?
items.e: Share equally, so divide: 175 ÷ 7. 1 is less than 7, so carry it: 17. 17 ÷ 7 = 2 R 3: write 2, carry 3 to make 35. 35 ÷ 7 = 5. Answer: 25. Check: 25 × 7 = 175. So the answer is 25 pages.

items.q: A Class 4 collects 252 cans for charity. They pack the cans equally into 6 boxes. How many cans go in each box?
items.e: Share equally, so divide: 252 ÷ 6. 2 is less than 6, so carry it: 25. 25 ÷ 6 = 4 R 1: write 4, carry 1 to make 12. 12 ÷ 6 = 2. Answer: 42. Check: 42 × 6 = 252. So the answer is 42 cans.

items.q: A school has 144 skates. They are put in pairs. How many pairs are there? Which number sentence solves it?
items.e: You know the total (144) and the size of each group (2), so divide the total by 2: 144 ÷ 2 = 72. 2 ÷ 144 divides the wrong way.

items.q: 84 students are put into teams of 7 for a football day. How many teams are there? Which number sentence solves it?
items.e: You know the total (84) and the size of each group (7), so divide the total by 7: 84 ÷ 7 = 12. 7 ÷ 84 divides the wrong way.

items.q: A farmer packs 96 eggs in cartons of 6. How many cartons does the farmer fill? Which number sentence solves it?
items.e: You know the total (96) and the size of each group (6), so divide the total by 6: 96 ÷ 6 = 16. 6 ÷ 96 divides the wrong way.

items.q: A school buys 6 boxes of 24 freezies. The freezies are shared equally among 8 classes. How many freezies does each class get?
items.e: Step 1: 6 × 24 = 144 freezies. Step 2: 144 ÷ 8 = 18 (14 ÷ 8 = 1 R 6, carry 6 to make 64; 64 ÷ 8 = 8). Each class gets 18 freezies.

items.q: 75 people go on a canoe trip in Algonquin Park. Each canoe holds 2 people. How many canoes are needed?
items.e: 75 ÷ 2 = 37 R 1. 37 canoes are not enough: 1 person is left. Round up to 38 canoes.

items.q: 118 campers go on an overnight trip. Each cabin sleeps 8 campers. How many cabins are needed?
items.e: 118 ÷ 8 = 14 R 6. 14 cabins are not enough: 6 campers are left. Round up to 15 cabins.

items.q: A farm stand has 230 apples. It packs them in bags of 4. How many bags can it fill completely?
items.e: 230 ÷ 4: 23 ÷ 4 = 5 R 3, carry 3 to make 30; 30 ÷ 4 = 7 R 2. So 230 ÷ 4 = 57 R 2. The 2 apples left over cannot fill a bag, so the answer is 57 bags.

items.q: A teacher shares 75 pencil crayons equally among 9 tables. Each table gets as many as possible. How many pencil crayons are left over?
items.e: 75 ÷ 9 = 8 R 3 (8 × 9 = 72, 75 − 72 = 3). The question asks how many are left over: 3 pencil crayons.

items.q: Siddharth has 100 loonies in a jar. He puts them in stacks of 6. How many loonies are not in a full stack?
items.e: 100 ÷ 6: 10 ÷ 6 = 1 R 4, carry 4 to make 40; 40 ÷ 6 = 6 R 4. So 100 ÷ 6 = 16 R 4. 16 stacks use 96 loonies, and 4 loonies are left over.

items.q: At a class party, 11 pizzas are shared equally by 4 tables. How many pizzas does each table get?
items.e: 11 ÷ 4 = 2 R 3. Each gets 2 pizzas. Each of the 3 pizzas left over is cut into 4 equal pieces. That makes 12 pieces, so each gets 3 pieces: 34 more. Answer: 2 34 pizzas. (Do not write the remainder as a decimal: 2 R 3 is not 2.3.)

items.q: Grandma bakes 7 loaves of bannock. She shares them equally among 3 families. How many loaves does each family get?
items.e: 7 ÷ 3 = 2 R 1. Each gets 2 loaves. The 1 loaf left over is cut into 3 equal pieces, so each gets 13 more. Answer: 2 13 loaves. (Do not write the remainder as a decimal: 2 R 1 is not 2.1.)

items.q: Kabir reads a 175-page book in 7 days. He reads the same number of pages each day. How many pages does he read each day?
items.e: Share equally, so divide: 175 ÷ 7. 1 is less than 7, so carry it: 17. 17 ÷ 7 = 2 R 3: write 2, carry 3 to make 35. 35 ÷ 7 = 5. Answer: 25. Check: 25 × 7 = 175. So the answer is 25 pages.

items.q: Meera has 100 loonies in a jar. She puts them in stacks of 6. How many loonies are not in a full stack?
items.e: 100 ÷ 6: 10 ÷ 6 = 1 R 4, carry 4 to make 40; 40 ÷ 6 = 6 R 4. So 100 ÷ 6 = 16 R 4. 16 stacks use 96 loonies, and 4 loonies are left over.
